text:
jess-support: FYI customer AcmeCloud on Private VPC reporting intermittent streaming resets and occasional 502/504 from our inference endpoint. Happens only from their VPC subnets, not from public internet. Symptoms: partial stream, then immediate RST from client side. Can reproduce from their infra intermittently.

sam-netops: Which endpoint IP/hostname and port are they hitting? Any recent SG/NACL changes on their side?

jess-support: Endpoint: api.redwood.example (TLS 443), model pinned to gptxx-13b-repl. Customer ran curl from app pod and got a few successful responses then: 
```
* TCP dump (client-side) snippet *
16:42:31.123456 IP 10.0.5.21.52345 > 34.200.111.22.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240
16:42:31.223555 IP 34.200.111.22.443 > 10.0.5.21.52345: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1
16:42:31.223600 IP 10.0.5.21.52345 > 34.200.111.22.443: Flags [.], ack 1
16:42:35.500100 IP 34.200.111.22.443 > 10.0.6.19.60121: Flags [R.], seq 0, ack 1  <-- host EIP differs (10.0.6.19 src)!
```
They see RST coming back to a different src/dst tuple (asymmetric). Not consistent every time.

maria-runtime: Asymmetric return path / SNAT variance will break connection tracking on stateful path or violate NACL expectations. Do we see multiple EIPs/NAT gateways on their egress?

jess-support: Customer confirmed two NAT gateways in different AZs, both attached to the same private routed subnets with a HA-floating route table. They said iptables SNAT is not used.

alex-sre: Can you paste their SG and NACL rules? Need to confirm ephemeral port ranges allowed (1024-65535) and that NACL has BOTH inbound+outbound ephemeral allowed. NACLs are stateless — if client uses ephemeral source port 52345, return must match and hit same NACL rules on return path.

jess-support: Customer NACL outbound: allow 0.0.0.0/0:443, ephemeral range 32768-61000 open only for outbound. Inbound they only allowed 443 from 0.0.0.0/0 and no explicit ephemeral range. Their SG allows 443 outbound and 443 inbound.

maria-runtime: That's the issue. With multiple NAT GW EIPs, the source port mapping on egress can change depending on which NAT handles the flow. If return hits a different NAT EIP or different AZ, the inbound NACL on that path may not allow the ephemeral source port. That results in silent drops or RSTs from intermediate devices. Also connection tracking entries on the NAT can expire if flows are idle for >timeout, causing later packets to be RSTed.

sam-netops: Quick checks for customer: 1) from pod run `curl --raw https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream` continuously to reproduce; 2) `sudo tcpdump -n -i any host 34.200.111.22 and port 443 -w /tmp/pcap.pcap` then share pcap; 3) capture `conntrack -L | grep 34.200.111.22` on NAT hosts if they manage them.

jess-support: They ran 10 minutes of curling, attached a small pcap. I uploaded excerpts: I see SYN -> SYN/ACK -> ACK then minutes later RST from a different src/dst.

eng-runtime-oncall: Paging in runtime team — tagging because if client traffic is SNATed to multiple EIPs and our load-balancer or backend sees different source IPs mid-stream, we may not correlate KV cache or streaming session state correctly. Could cause partial stream rejections.

maria-runtime: Two-pronged mitigation: 1) Customer: tighten routing so egress uses single NAT EIP (or use a single NAT per pool) OR open full ephemeral port range (1024-65535) on NACL inbound/outbound so any SNAT mapping is allowed. 2) If they need high-availability NATs, use AWS Transit Gateway or NAT with Elastic IP per AZ and ensure symmetric routing. Also suggest enabling VPC endpoint for the Redwood control plane so traffic doesn't leave the AZ.

alex-sre: Additional band-aid: increase conntrack timeouts on NAT hosts for established TCP (e.g., tcp-timeout) so long-lived streams don't get torn down mid-stream. But that's only a temp fix.

sam-netops: Also confirm no TCP offload / middlebox rewriting TLS SNI or doing TLS inspection — that could cause immediate TLS handshake failures.

jess-support: Customer confirmed no TLS inspect appliance. They changed NACL inbound to allow ephemeral range on both inbound/outbound and pinned egress to one NAT EIP for the app subnet. After change they reported stable streaming for 30m, no RSTs so far.

alex-sre: Good. Can we get the customer's final confirmation and a copy of the pcap + their NAT/GW config for our postmortem? Also recommend they monitor `conntrack -S` metrics on their NAT/GW for expirations.

jess-support: I'll ask for artifacts and let them know suggested permanent recommended architecture (single SNAT per session or symmetric routing). Will update ticket and close once we have pcap + confirmation.

opsbot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0543, severity: medium, owner: jess-support, notes: suspected asymmetric NAT/SNAT + NACL ephemeral port omission.

eng-runtime-oncall: Thanks team. If customer sees regression after we close, escalate and we'll run focused packet-inspection from our side.

jess-support: thanks, closing loop with customer now. :wave:
